body:
`case_study:pc-jeweller-2018` | 2018-05-04 | tickers: PCJEWELLER | confidence: verified

PC Jeweller hit a high of ~Rs 600 on 16 Jan 2018 (pre-2024 split prices), fell 42% in a month during the Feb 2018 Nirav Modi/PNB jewellery-sector contagion, then crashed again in Apr-May 2018 when the promoter gifted shares to family members via off-market transfers (~$2.7 bn of m-cap lost at the worst point). A buyback announced to calm markets was withdrawn in Jul 2018 (-43% in a week to ~Rs 68). Mid-2018 low ~Rs 95 then further to the teens/single digits by 2020; the company defaulted on ~Rs 3,400-3,466 cr of bank loans (2021-22) and SBI sought insolvency. A 2024 settlement with lenders sparked a speculative rally. Visible flags: (1) inventory and receivables (export receivables, UAE) rising much faster than sales; CFO weak or negative for years despite reported profits; (2) heavy gold-metal-loan/working-capital debt; (3) links to Vakrangee (itself under SEBI scrutiny), which held PCJ shares; (4) promoter share 'gifts' and poor disclosure; (5) buyback withdrawal = management credibility loss. Lesson: in jewellery, inventory days and receivable days are the forensic key; a gold retailer reporting profits but no cash is suspect. Insolvency-adjacent rallies are not turnarounds until debt is actually extinguished.

**Lesson:** Inventory + receivable days decide jewellery quality
**Spotted early by:** market sellers after promoter gift disclosure
